name: Imperial Novel route registry
scope: Source-audited route inventory with one runtime registry driving Worker page-shell dispatch, canonical aliases, noindex policy, and static sitemap paths. The registry also records initial source-backed access, locale/RTL, and navigation policies. It does not certify every API method/object-ownership rule, mixed-language per-chapter locale behavior, live HTTP/browser behavior, or global rights-gated product switches.
knownOpenQuestions: /fandom/:slug is a compatibility redirect, not a dedicated fandom landing.
/discover canonicalizes to /catalog in the runtime route registry; deployed canonical response verification remains open.
/for-you canonicalizes to /made-for-you in the runtime route registry; deployed canonical response verification remains open.
Shared discoveryPage renderers require per-feature functional and authorization tests.
HTTP method and object-level permissions are not certified by this UI route manifest.
Production status, active assets, cache behavior and browser navigation remain unverified.
Route-level authentication and role requirements must be reconciled against client navigation guards and API method/object authorization; this shell map does not certify them.
Canonical, locale/RTL, and navigation exposure policies are now registered and source-tested; deployed browser verification remains open.

Worker sitemap routes and XML output now have mock-D1 integration coverage for static paths, publication/rights query filters, pagination and output URLs; live D1 and deployed sitemap verification remain open.
Live Worker behavior, HTTP status codes, browser navigation, and deployed asset versions require runtime verification.

/omniportal is publicly linked and included in the static sitemap; external search is limited to enabled authorized connectors and imports require authentication plus an enabled authorized connector. Confirm whether a global product-level disable switch is required before treating the portal as fully off.
Reader chapter-content and single/batch unlock source guards are now inventoried and regression-tested; runtime integration and concurrency tests remain open.

Reader direction is based on the novel-level language field. If a single novel may contain chapters in different languages, a chapter-level language override and corresponding API field will be needed.

OmniPortal currently appears in both the desktop top navigation and main navigation drawer and remains in the static sitemap. The required global disable state pending rights approval still needs an explicit product-level decision and implementation.
Unknown page paths now resolve to a real HTTP 404 and noindex response in source; deployed HTTP status verification remains open.
API authorization registry and source tests now cover all exact API declarations plus dynamic API patterns; seeded-D1 adversarial tests and optional-session response-shape tests remain open.

canonicalPolicy.implementation: src/route-canonical.mjs plus Worker html() metadata injection

localePolicy.uiDirection: The selected interface language controls document-level direction.
localePolicy.readerContentDirection: The novel/work language controls the readerContent element direction independently of the selected interface language.
localePolicy.languageStorage: imperial_language in localStorage; routes do not use locale prefixes.
localePolicy.scope: Current content direction is work-level because the current reader obtains language from the novel record; per-chapter language overrides for mixed-language works are not established.
